issues.description: The UML in the problem statement defines Animal with two attributes (name: String, age: int) and a constructor Animal(String, int), but the provided solution implements Animal with only a single-argument constructor Animal(String) and no age attribute. This constructor/attribute mismatch can confuse students about which constructor to implement and whether an age field is required.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the specification and the implementation. Either (A) update the UML/specification to require only a name and a single-argument constructor Animal(String), or (B) add the age attribute and change the Animal constructor in the solution/template to Animal(String, int) (and update get/set methods accordingly). Be explicit in the problem text which constructor signature and attributes students must implement.

issues.description: The problem statement text says 'All three animals have something in common: they have a name.' (implying only a name is required), but the UML earlier declares an age attribute for Animal (age: int). This internal contradiction in the problem statement about Animal's attributes can lead to confusion whether students should implement an age field.
issues.suggestedFix: Clarify the problem statement to consistently list the Animal attributes. Remove the age attribute from the UML if it is not required, or update the textual description to state that Animal has both name and age and require students to implement both (including constructor, getters, and setters).
